name: mon16-3
why: A close officer vote and a disastrous final read make this compelling, though repeated arguments slow the middle.

moments.text: Haiku treats a killer's accusation as proof that her partner is innocent.
The town votes out the real officer by a single vote.
Opus names Sonnet as Luna's partner, putting both killers in danger.

dull.why: Sol and Luna repeat the claim and denial without adding much.
The final three restate their positions several times before voting.

irony.evidence: I need Sol voted out today or Luna's cover is blown and I'm next.

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Sol 4 (Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Luna); Luna 3 (Sol, Terra, Opus)

mistake.evidence: Luna named Sonnet, so Sonnet isn't her partner.

voices.evidence: I'm not shielding Sol, I'm trapping him.

clash.evidence: Sonnet spends every line defending Luna by attacking Haiku. That's a partner's work.

freshness.evidence: Vote Luna and her card settles my claim.

ending.evidence: I trusted Luna's accusation as clearance, and I pushed Terra out
